experience.player_does: Launch the game and inspect a map probe containing circle, right-angle triangle, half-cell, and corner cells in all quarter-turn orientations.
experience.feels_like: The new primitives should make the cell language more expressive without changing the existing square and triangle compositions or the seamless world presentation.
experience.camera: Keep the existing fixed logical viewport, fullscreen surface, cell pitch, and map framing.
experience.controls: No new controls; the probe is authored content and remains visible through the existing PLAY flow and optional F2 grid aid.
experience.not_this: Not a replacement for the existing isosceles TR shape, not a new map format version, not layered geometry inside one cell, and not a final claim that all four shapes belong permanently.

design_refs.why: The settled cell grammar says the vocabulary grows one primitive at a time and gains orientations through draw-time rotation; this slice tests four named candidates within that rule.
The probe must be judged in the established 15-unit fullscreen presentation without changing the amount of world visible.
The probe remains ordinary versioned map content using the existing strict token boundary and no new persisted format.

considered_existing.why_not: It already owns shape IDs, token mapping, and reusable polygon geometry, so extending it avoids a second primitive registry.
It already translates catalogued shape tokens into packed cell codes, so adding aliases there keeps typed callers independent of raw token parsing.
Its generic polygon renderer already rotates and draws any catalogued geometry, so no renderer fork is needed.
The existing authored map is the established visual probe surface and can host the new examples without changing the document format.
The existing catalog test is the right place to verify IDs and polygon geometry for the expanded vocabulary.

modules.role: Own the typed primitive catalog and packed-cell aliases for the four new shape candidates.
modules.why: The parser and renderer already meet at this catalog boundary; extending it keeps shape identity and geometry in one place.
modules.boundary_data: Maps persisted shape tokens to typed integer codes and returns normalized polygon points for rendering.

modules.role: Provide authored examples of each candidate and its rotations in the existing map.
modules.why: The shape batch must be judged in the same authored surface as the existing compositions.
modules.boundary_data: Versioned JSON tokens consumed by LevelFormat and LevelLayer.

modules.role: Verify the catalog and authored map accept the expanded shape vocabulary.
modules.why: New persisted tokens must be rejected when unknown and round-trip correctly when catalogued.
modules.boundary_data: Constructs typed catalog and level values and observes codes, polygons, and validation results.

files.why: Add circle, right-angle triangle, half-cell rectangle, and corner IDs, tokens, and normalized polygon geometry while retaining existing shapes.
Expose typed constants for the new catalogued shapes alongside the existing shape aliases.
Add a visible four-shape probe with quarter-turn examples to the existing authored map without changing its version or dimensions.
Verify each new token resolves to known geometry and that the polygon point counts distinguish the candidates.

functions.why: Register normalized polygon points for the four new primitives in the catalog.
Resolve the new persisted two-character shape tokens without changing the existing token boundary.
Extend validation to recognize the new catalog range.
Continue exposing packed shape identity to typed callers after the catalog range grows.
